lede: Round 14 read, on one fight each, that the two choices the gangs' table rests on had flipped: switching encircle on seemed to finish the enemy, and the lure seemed to cost the pack. This page re-measures both over 16 paired fights per opponent on the yard and the Terminus (8 seeds each), with only the table differing. Nothing changes in the game until you choose.
recommendation: Keep the table as shipped (encircle off, bait on). Over seeds neither flip helps on your maps. Encircle on leaves a standard element stronger in 11 of 16 fights and the pack nearly wiped (6% left against 17%). Flipping both is worse against chasers in 14 of 16 fights. Bait on or off is a coin toss everywhere except the drills' own test lane. Round 14's one-fight readings were noise.

arms.shipped: Best or tied against every opponent on your maps: wins all 16 fights against dug-in guns with the most of the pack left, and leaves chasers at 42% and a standard element at 39%.
arms.encircle: No gain against guns, slightly worse against chasers (enemy stronger in 10 of 16 fights), and a clear loss against a standard element: the pack ends at 6% (enemy stronger in 11 of 16 fights).
arms.nobait: A coin toss against chasers (enemy left lower in 9 fights, higher in 7) and against a standard element (8 to 7). Identical to shipped against guns, where the lure never fires.
arms.both: The worst against chasers: the enemy is left stronger in 14 of 16 fights, and the pack is almost always wiped out.

method: Measured on builder0 at stream/squad e676c481–da298860 (identical game behaviour), make squad-doctrine-series: the gang pack (an IFV leader and three scouts) against each opponent, 90 s or until one side is gone, seeds 1–8 on the yard and on the Terminus, every arm on the same seeds (same starts, same fire dice). Pack and enemy left are hull plus shield as a share of the start, averaged over the 16 fights. The last column counts paired fights where the enemy ended weaker or stronger than under the shipped table, with a two-sided sign test. Includes this round's far-ambush fix (the flanker no longer circles), which every arm shares. Frames: the drills' own lane at your camera pose, 10 s in.
